blocks.text: I can understand what someone wants to do and say what I want to do in Lanzarote in the summer.

items.title: Say what I {want} to do and react

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A verb meaning to want, wanting.
I want. Part of the verb querer.
You want. Part of the verb querer.
She, he, it wants. Part of the verb querer.

blocks.text: Sofía and Quique’s mum, Elena, is organising a family trip to Lanzarote.

items: Lanzarote is an island. It is one of the Islas Canarias (the Canary Islands), to the west of Africa.
In Lanzarote there is an airport, lots of ports, a stadium, and a long coast with lots of pretty beaches.

blocks.text: Lanzarote is famous for these places.
It is typical to eat ‘papas arrugadas’ with ‘mojo picón’, a delicious sauce.
These words are useful for talking about the trip. Match each Spanish word to its English meaning.
The verb querer does not follow the general rules. ‘Quer-’ changes to ‘quier-’.
The endings are the same as for all -er verbs. They match the person of the verb.
To say someone wants to do something, use the right form of querer. Then use the **infinitive** straight after it.

items: Quiero {nadar} en el mar. = I want to swim in the sea.
Quiere {ver} el río. = She wants to see the river.
Quiero {probar} churros. = I want to try churros.
Quiero {comer} muchas tapas. = I want to eat many tapas.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: In English we say ‘want **to** do’. In Spanish you do not need a word for ‘to’. Just use the correct form of querer and the infinitive.

options: I want to go to a festival.
She wants to go to a festival.
You want to go to a festival.
You want to learn about the culture.
I want to learn about the culture.
She wants to learn about the culture.

items.q: Quiero comprar la ropa en el mercado.
options: She wants to buy clothes at the market.
You want to buy clothes at the market.
I want to buy clothes at the market.

items.q: I want to eat many tapas.
She wants to see the volcano.

blocks.text: To give an opinion, use **es** and an adjective. Tap each adjective to see its meaning.
Sofía says what she wants to do. Quique gives his opinion.

items: Quiero visitar el volcán. — Yo también. {Es interesante.}
Quiero ver un jardín de cactus. — ¡Yo no! {¡Es aburrido!}

blocks.label: What do you notice?
blocks.text: Quique’s opinions start with **es** and then an adjective: es interesante, es aburrido.

items: Sound-spelling correspondences can be practised through reading and cultural learning about Lanzarote.
Querer means to want, wanting: **quiero** (I want), **quieres** (you want), **quiere** (she, he, it wants).
To say someone wants to do something, use the right form of querer followed by an **infinitive**.
To give an opinion, use **es** and an adjective.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Lanzarote in summer: 2-verb phrases with ‘querer’
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a short answer. Write the Spanish words in lower case.

questions.prompt: Write ‘I want’ in Spanish (a form of querer).
Write ‘you want’ in Spanish (a form of querer).
Write ‘she wants’ in Spanish (a form of querer).
Complete: ‘Quiero ___ en el mar.’ (I want to swim in the sea.) Write the infinitive.
questions.explanation: After quiero we use an infinitive: nadar.

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘Quiero ver el volcán’.
questions.answer: i want to see the volcano
questions.explanation: Quiero means ‘I want’ and ver el volcán means ‘to see the volcano’.

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘Quiere ir a la playa’.
questions.answer: she wants to go to the beach
accepted: he wants to go to the beach

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘I want to eat many tapas’.
questions.explanation: Use quiero for ‘I want’, then the infinitive comer.

questions.prompt: What does ‘nunca’ mean in English? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: ‘Lanzarote nunca es aburrido’ means ‘Lanzarote is never boring’.

questions.prompt: What does ‘a menudo’ mean in English? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: ‘A menudo, hay un mercado en la plaza’ means ‘Often, there is a market in the square’.

questions.prompt: Lanzarote is one of the ___ Islands. Which islands? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: Lanzarote is an island of the Islas Canarias (the Canary Islands), to the west of Africa.
